page_language_translations_licenses: On Spanish, Russian, French and German pages the reader shows a translation in that language where Sefaria has one we have reviewed. The French Bible du Rabbinat (1899) and the German translations by Wohlgemuth, Hirsch, Zunz and Bamberger and the Berlin Mishnah edition are in the public domain. The Spanish Tanaj Español, translated by Rav Yehuda Ribco (serjudio.com), is used under the CC BY-NC-ND license, and the Russian Torah translation by Dr. Dmitri Slivniak, edited by Dr. Itzhak Streshinsky (Da Project, 2011), is used under the CC BY-NC license. Sh'elah is non-commercial and shows both unchanged. Neither may be reused for commercial purposes.

the_following_libraries_are_used_in: The following libraries are used in the Service's own frontend code and are each MIT-licensed. See each project's own repository for the full license text:
the_text_typefaces_cardo_and_inter: Sh'elah's own typefaces are Newsreader (Production Type), Hanken Grotesk (Alfredo Marco Pradil) and Frank Ruhl Libre (Yanek Iontef, after Rafael Frank's classic design). All three are licensed under the SIL Open Font License (OFL) 1.1 and are served from this site, not from Google Fonts. The OFL permits embedding, use, redistribution and modification, provided the fonts are not sold on their own.
this_obligation_is_not_limited_to: This obligation is not limited to a user's own downstream reuse. It also covers Sh'elah's own act of serving an AI Output. Where an AI Output substantially synthesizes retrieved Wikipedia content (the last-resort case described in the AI Disclosure page), that specific answer is treated as CC-BY-SA Adapted Material of the underlying Wikipedia passage: it is attributed to Wikipedia and made available under CC-BY-SA 4.0 for that specific answer. This overrides the general 'personal use only' Content license in the Terms of Service §9, which does not apply to this subset of AI Output. This is a deliberately conservative operator choice, adopted 2026-09-06 without a definitive legal determination of whether such synthesis actually creates an 'Adapted Material' obligation under CC BY-SA 4.0 §1.1. The choice was made because treating the obligation as applicable carries less risk than assuming it does not.
torah_talmud_halachic_and_commentary_tex: Torah, Talmud, halachic, and commentary texts are retrieved live from the Sefaria API. Much of the Sefaria corpus is licensed CC-BY or is public domain, but licensing varies by text, and some texts on Sefaria carry more restrictive terms. Sh'elah displays Sefaria content under Sefaria's own terms of use. Verify the license of any specific text on Sefaria before reusing it outside this app. See Sefaria's licensing page for the authoritative, per-text breakdown.
used_only_as_a_last_resort: Used only as a last-resort general-knowledge source when Judaic texts and computed calendar data cannot answer a question. Wikipedia content is licensed CC-BY-SA, which carries a share-alike obligation. Any downstream reuse of Wikipedia-sourced material retrieved through this app must itself be licensed CC-BY-SA and attributed to Wikipedia. See Wikipedia's reuse guide for the full terms.
whitelisted_external_halachic_sources_us: Whitelisted external halachic sources used as second-tier evidence (after Sefaria and before general web sources). Each carries its own site terms of use; Sh'elah links to and quotes brief excerpts from these sources under fair-use / attribution norms, not a blanket relicense.
zmanim_0_3_1_used_in: zmanim 0.3.1 (used in the Service's zmanim/halachic-times calculation engine, backend/zmanim_engine.py) is not a simple permissive license. Its installed package metadata declares the GNU Lesser General Public License v2 or later (LGPLv2+). LGPLv2+ is a "weak copyleft" library license: this project's own code may use the library and remain under its own MIT license (dynamic use/import doesn't trigger the copyleft), but redistributing the zmanim package itself would carry LGPL obligations, including making the LGPL-covered source available and, per LGPLv2 §6, allowing the library to be replaced or relinked with a modified version. No modifications to zmanim's own source are made in this repo.
